key_insight: ADfiRe combines empirical correlations and CFD-informed parameterizations with an advection–diffusion–reaction thermal model to predict wildfire spread while balancing physical detail and computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets rapid wildfire forecasting across multiple fuel types and arbitrary topography while accounting for wind-driven flame tilting.
method: Integrate fuel databases, empirical correlations, and CFD-informed parameterizations into a physics-based transport model.
Couple solid-fuel pyrolysis with oxygen-limited char/volatile combustion using two-stage Arrhenius kinetics.
Model wind effects using a Byram-number formulation to distinguish plume- and wind-dominated propagation.
evidence_signal: Validation against five field-scale experimental fires in Mediterranean shrublands showed quantitative agreement in rate of spread and fireline intensity.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify runtime or establish validation beyond Mediterranean shrublands, leaving real-time performance and broader generalization to be assessed.
paper_title: ADfiRe: An empirical- and CFD-informed advection-diffusion-reaction thermal model for wildfire spread
